claims.text: The packaged memo field map is the reply's 13 fields in order, with M18 right after M2 in the turnover field and business details, loan request, credit history, key risks and the recommendation left unmapped. A malformed field map (an unknown figure, a placeholder mismatch, a judgement field mapping a figure, a repeated key, bad YAML) is refused, naming the problem.

P14, P20 and the snapshot (invariants). The preview text passes the grounding guard, each account against its own figures and policy result: on every synthetic archetype and profile with every feature, with the policy check shown and hidden; on a two-account demo case with an override, a profile name, negative balances and n/a figures. A literal number in a firm's template fails the guard. With show_policy_verdict on, every section showing an outcome holds the illustrative label, the label is the first line of the policy-check section after the memo fields, and the recommendation is empty. With it off, there is no outcome, rule result or [Rn] tag. Changing each R22 input changes the snapshot hash: a statement, the ruleset, the firm rules, the profile, the override log, the thresholds, the field map, the policy hash, show_policy_verdict and the package version. A preview writes no file but one preview entry in the case log, holding hashes only.

All T24 tests pass, including the R27 unmapped-field marks, the R48 demo stamp, determinism, the refusal for a case with no statement, and the cma case preview CLI (exit 0 with the snapshot; exit 1 when the guard fails; exit 2 when refused).

claims.proof_cmd: python3 -m pytest -q -x -p no:cacheprovider && ruff check src tests

notes: Committed as 03379db on the T24 worktree branch. The full-suite run came before one small edit in pack._build: the snapshot's statement hashes now cover every account the figures layer returns, not only accounts that have lines. tests/test_preview.py was re-run after that edit (34 passed). Design choices: section text quotes money to the whole pound via Metric.display (R2, D230). Policy-check rule lines do not quote the policy's rule descriptions, because they hold untagged digits the guard would refuse. Each rule line gives its id, the figure tagged [Mn], and each limit tagged [Rn] after a limit word. Several accounts are prefixed 'Account <key>:', and each account's text is guarded against its own figures. Known edge, Tier 2 only: an account key made only of digits would be read by the guard as an untagged number, and the preview would report itself ungrounded. Firm rules are not built yet (T37), so the snapshot hashes firm_rules.yaml's bytes, or null when it is absent. The override log position is the number of override records together with the hash of overrides.jsonl. The case-log head is left out of the snapshot because R22 does not list it, and the preview's own entry would change it. When the guard fails, the preview entry is still recorded, with grounded false; T27 is to refuse sign-off on it.
